done_when: A forge board server with no page open for 30 minutes stops by itself and says so. While no page is open it does not fetch from GitHub or rebuild the board. An open page keeps it running.

known.title: Not done: While no page is open it does not fetch from GitHub or rebuild the board.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - starting `forge board` before any page connects.
The live command still unconditionally fetches origin at src/forge/board.py:69, before entering `board_server.serve()` at line 78. Guarding the server's periodic fetch therefore leaves startup fetching without an open page, contrary to the Done-when requirement. Defer this live-server fetch until a page connects. The new test misses it because its audit hook matches only the literal executable `git` (tests/test_board_page_lifetime.py:42), whereas repo.run resolves Git to an absolute executable path (src/forge/repo.py:225,251). Correct that observation so the existing no-page assertion detects this failure.
findings.title: Not done: While no page is open it does not fetch from GitHub or rebuild the board.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a board starts and nobody ever opens its page.
The startup-without-a-page phase advances only 1,790 seconds, then opens streams. The only shutdown assertion occurs after those streams close. Consequently, this proof never checks that an entirely unattended server exits after 30 minutes from launch; it would pass if shutdown worked only after a page had connected and closed. Exercise an invocation that crosses the startup idle deadline without opening any stream and assert its exit and explanation.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_no_page_pauses_work_and_stops_after_thirty_minutes

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round: repair the fetch at start and prove the case where nobody ever opens the page.

why: Each forge board starts a new live server that never stops and keeps working with no page open, so copies pile up and use CPU (GitHub issue 1282).
